Read a large dataset in repeatable blocks of rows

Source: R/source.R
fastglm_source.Rd

A source describes how to obtain a block of observations when a fitting function needs it. This permits repeated model-fitting passes without loading the complete dataset into memory. The supplied function, called a callback, receives the block number and returns its observations.

fastglm_source(
  callback,
  n_chunks,
  reset = NULL,
  formula = NULL,
  prototype = NULL,
  weights = NULL,
  offset = NULL
)

Arguments

callback

function of chunk index returning a data frame, or a list with `X`, `y`, and optional `weights` and `offset`. Two-component models may also supply `Z` for the binary design and a list of `count` and `zero` offsets; otherwise `Z` defaults to `X` and a vector offset applies to the count or positive-outcome component.

n_chunks

positive number of chunks.

reset

optional function called before chunk one on every pass.

formula

optional model formula for data-frame blocks. A formula such as `y ~ x | z` specifies separate count/positive and binary designs.

prototype

example data frame defining all intended factor levels and transformations; it need not contain all observations.

weights, offset

optional column names in data-frame blocks. For a two-component formula, two offset column names supply count/positive and binary offsets, respectively.

Value

A `fastglm_source` object for [fastglm_streaming()], [fastglm_ordinal_streaming()], or the count and two-part fitting functions.

Details

When a formula is supplied, `prototype` is an example data frame used to establish the design columns, factor levels, and transformations. This recorded specification, called the schema, is reused for every block so that a column has the same meaning throughout the analysis. For splines and other data-dependent transformations, the prototype must establish the intended basis, including knots and boundary knots.
